validated_results.journal: European journal of cancer prevention : the official journal of the European Cancer Prevention Organisation (ECP)
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study reporting an odds ratio for cumulative tea consumption and incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest tertile of cumulative tea consumption (population controls)

sample_size.excerpt: The analysis was restricted to the subset of men, aged 45-70 years, who underwent interviews in which aspects of lifelong consumption of non-alcoholic beverages were ascertained. There were 399 incident cases of prostate cancer, 476 population controls and 621 cancer controls.
sample_size.location: Abstract, results sentence; total_n derived from reported group counts 399 + 476 + 621 = 1496

cases.excerpt: There were 399 incident cases of prostate cancer, 476 population controls and 621 cancer controls.

effect_size.excerpt: Among daily tea drinkers, the odds ratio associated with the highest tertile of cumulative consumption was 2.0 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.3-3.0) when using population controls and 1.6 (95% CI 1.0-2.4) when using cancer controls. In conclusion, the consumption of coffee or carbonated beverages does not influence the risk of prostate cancer.
